items.title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected, complicating Fed's inflation fight
items.summary: The report comes at a critical juncture for the Federal Reserve as it considers its next move regarding interest rates.
items.body: Costs for goods and services rose more than expected in October, providing fresh warning signs for the Federal Reserve in its fight to lower inflation. The consumer price index , a broad gauge of costs across the U.S. economy, increased a seasonally adjusted 0.4% for the month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had been looking for a 0.3% increase. Stripping out volatile food and energy, so-called core CPI increased 0.3% against the forecast for a 0.2% gain. The report comes at a critical juncture for the Federal Reserve as it considers its next interest-rate move.

items.title: CoreWeave earnings put debt-fueled AI build-out under scrutiny
items.summary: CoreWeave’s earnings after the bell could calm fears about its debt-fueled AI buildout — or stoke more fear.
items.body: CoreWeave faces a pivotal test when it reports its third-quarter financial results after the bell on Tuesday. The market will be closely watching what the neocloud company says about artificial intelligence spending — and how it plans to finance its infrastructure buildout. The outcome could either calm concerns over its debt or stoke more fear. "Investors need neoclouds to quantify how much financing they expect to raise to execute on existing backlog," Wolfe Research said in a note Monday. "We think outlooks that communicate when and which avenues of funding will be tapped will increase investor confidence." CoreWeave stock and bonds have come under pressure as fears deepened about the enormous amount of debt it has taken out to build its data centers. Its stock is down roughly 40% over the past month.

items.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
items.summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
items.body: Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the affair between its chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy. Jensen Huang, a co-founder of Nvidia who has led it to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. She was an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia. Nvidia said on Tuesday that Wachtell attorney Joon Kim was set to lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into Jensen Huang's affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe. Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the US artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools.

items.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
items.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.
items.body: As Nvidia , one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy , attention is turning to the much smaller company she worked for. Alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing company. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba. According to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the company advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations.

items.title: Philip R. Lane: The science and practice of monetary policy communication: the ECB experience
items.body: I will divide this speech into two parts. In the first part, I will review recent contributions by ECB staff on the science of monetary policy communication. These indicators can also be employed to test whether central bank communication follows systematic patterns that reflect the economic outlook and the policy stance. Indeed, the evidence suggests that central banks tend to communicate in a systematic manner, following “communication rules”. [ 8 ] By estimating a systematic relationship between the tone of communication on monetary policy, economic activity and inflation, ECB staff find that, in line with our primary objective of price stability, ECB communication on monetary policy systematically places more emphasis on inflation developments (Chart 1, panel b).

items.title: Before Xi and Trump’s Apec meeting, what’s on hold – and what’s on the table?
items.summary: China has announced the extension of suspensions on a slew of trade measures against the United States on Monday, following a similar move by Washington days earlier, maintaining the bilateral trade truce ahead of a planned leaders’ summit. The arrangement was initially due to…
items.body: China has announced the extension of suspensions on a slew of trade measures against the United States on Monday, following a similar move by Washington days earlier, maintaining the bilateral trade truce ahead of a planned leaders’ summit. The arrangement was initially due to expire on November 10. Following negotiations in September, both sides agreed to extend the truce – brokered in Busan last year – by two months until January 10, 2027. The decision comes before President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump are expected to meet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen next week, their third meeting this year. Here, we look at what specific measures were paused and where the US-China trade truce stands now.

items.title: Schumer accuses Trump of defending Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at cost of national security
items.summary: Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., the Republican chairman of the Select Committee on China and told CNBC he expects answers about Jensen Huang's relationship.
items.body: Democratic leader Sen. Charles Schumer ripped President Donald Trump on Tuesday for defending embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the expense of U.S. national security. "The press reports that Trump was briefed more than a year ago that Nvidia's CEO was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and Trump didn't do anything – anything – about it," Schumer, D-N.Y., said on the Senate floor. Schumer's broadside came on the heels of New York Times reports that Trump had been briefed about Huang's extramarital affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang — whom U.S. intelligence concluded was a spy for China — and opted not to do anything about it.

items.title: The AI pay gap: A chip boom breeds jealousy and labor unrest in Asia
items.body: PYEONGTAEK, South Korea/TAIPEI/HONG KONG -- "Welcome to the world's semiconductor capital" reads a sign on the gate of a Samsung Electronics chip plant in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, a 20-minute express train ride from southern Seoul. Thousands of employees were at work there one November afternoon, while more manufacturing facilities were under construction close by to meet soaring demand for advanced memory chips, critical components for artificial intelligence computing.

items.title: China's goods surplus tops $1 trillion for a second year amid calls for Beijing to rebalance trade
items.summary: China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion as of October, potentially intensifying complaints from trading partners already wary over the glut of cheap Chinese goods.
items.body: China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion this year with two months to spare, at a time when partner countries have been raising concerns over Beijing's exports that have been undercutting local industries. For the 10 months through October, the surplus reached $1.04 trillion, compared with a record $1.2 trillion for the full year 2025, when it crossed the $1 trillion mark for the first time, customs data on Tuesday showed. That milestone came as calls from trading partners have grown louder for Beijing to boost domestic demand and balance its economy. The International Monetary Fund has also repeatedly urged China to accelerate its pivot from relying on exports for growth toward a model powered by domestic consumption.

items.title: Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
items.summary: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
items.body: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month. It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times. The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity". It is floating at a volatile time for big tech firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

items.title: French police raid Ritz hotel in Mohamed Al Fayed sexual abuse investigation
items.summary: Arrests made after three properties were searched in relation to inquiry into late businessman French police have made arrests after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris , in relation to an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al…
items.body: French police have made arrests after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris , in relation to an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al Fayed. Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released, according to the Paris public prosecutor’s office. Another property in Paris and one in Saint-Tropez, both with links to Fayed, were also searched in mid-October. Several of Fayed’s alleged victims were also interviewed by officers from the organised crime division of the Paris prosecutor’s office. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into “allegations of human trafficking committed by an organised group, aggravated pimping committed by an organised group, and rape”.

items.title: Piero Cipollone: Cash and the digital euro: two sides of the same coin
items.body: It is a pleasure to be back here for the first time since the Parliament adopted its position on the Single Currency Package, and I very much welcome the broad support it received in the plenary session on 9 July. This gives a strong democratic backing to the digital euro. Let me also thank you for the considerable work and constructive dialogue that have made this progress possible. A swift conclusion of the ongoing trilogue negotiations would pave the way for the adoption of the Single Currency Package [ 1 ] by the end of the year as foreseen in the One Europe, One Market Roadmap . [ 2 ] This would give us the legal certainty needed to complete our preparations for the digital euro. It would also give certainty to the market regarding the planned date for a possible first issuance, which can be set only after the Regulation is adopted.

items.title: Iranian delegation at China import expo says ‘indirect trade’ has grown since war began
items.summary: The resilience of Beijing-Tehran ties has allowed “indirect trade” between China and Iran to boom, even though the US-Israel war on Iran has entered its ninth month and American sanctions are complicating transactions, Iranian trade officials said in Shanghai. But executives…
items.body: The resilience of Beijing-Tehran ties has allowed “indirect trade” between China and Iran to boom, even though the US-Israel war on Iran has entered its ninth month and American sanctions are complicating transactions, Iranian trade officials said in Shanghai. But executives from Iran’s oil and energy sector attending a major trade show in the eastern Chinese city said impeded passage through the Strait of Hormuz continued to choke oil shipments to China. “There is more ‘indirect trade’ flowing between the two countries [since the war started in February],” an official from the Iran Trade Centre (ITC) in China said.

items.title: White House vows to press ahead with tariffs despite midterm backlash over rising prices
items.summary: Business executives warned at a Washington summit of rising costs and shifting supply chains as polls showed growing opposition to Trump's tariffs.
items.body: One week after voters punished Republicans over rising prices in the midterm elections , President Donald Trump's White House signaled it would stay the course on tariffs , even as his former top economic advisor warned that Americans are footing the bill. Jim Goyer, Trump's director of White House Office of Public Liaison, defended tariffs as a tool to rebuild U.S. manufacturing, secure supply chains and protect national security during an address Tuesday at the B20 summit , a gathering of global business leaders in Washington hosted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. "And we are just getting started," Goyer said. "Our ambition is to continue this pace for the remainder of the president's term in office." But Gary Cohn , who served as Trump's chief economic advisor during his first administration, offered a sharply different assessment during an onstage interview later Tuesday.

items.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
items.summary: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
items.body: Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates. Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator. The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks. However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying. The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

items.title: US inflation rose 0.4% in October as price increases cooled and gas costs dipped
items.summary: New data comes after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.…
items.body: US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year-over-year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown. But the newest data shows that prices are still increasing at a moderate pace. Economists estimate that, if interpolating the data for October 2025, the topline inflation figure for October 2026 would have been 3.9%, according to Oxford Economics . That would have been the highest its been since May 2026, when inflation reached 4.2%, a three-year high. Higher energy costs driven by the Iran war have been the main factor behind increased inflation.

items.title: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser strikes bullish tone on China expansion after brokerage approval
items.summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser has struck a confident and optimistic note that the US lender would become a leading investment bank in mainland China after it received approval to set up a wholly-owned securities firm in one of the world’s largest capital markets. Beijing’s…
items.body: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser has struck a confident and optimistic note that the US lender would become a leading investment bank in mainland China after it received approval to set up a wholly-owned securities firm in one of the world’s largest capital markets. Beijing’s supportive stance on foreign financial service firms as well as China’s strength in manufacturing and artificial intelligence would also offer opportunities for Citi as it pursued fresh growth engines, Fraser said at the Citi China Conference in Shanghai on Tuesday. “I think an awful lot of things and challenges can be overcome with growth and with revenue that will certainly help the transitions take place.” The CEO added that Citi had already seen revenue potential from AI in China.

items.title: Here's the inflation breakdown for October 2026 — in one chart
items.summary: The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, a reduction from September but a level economists said is still uncomfortably high.
items.body: Inflation throttled back in October from its blistering pace in September amid a more moderate rise in gasoline prices, but remained high as categories like food and housing put upward pressure on consumer prices. The consumer price index, an inflation barometer, rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, after adjusting for seasonal factors, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday. That's down from 0.6% in September but higher than the 0.3% that economists expected . "It's uncomfortably high," said Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's. "The Fed's not going to be happy about it. It certainly makes it more likely we get another rate increase in December." The Federal Reserve uses inflation data to guide its interest rate policy. The U.S. central bank raised rates in September amid a recent pickup in inflation, which economists largely attribute to the war in Iran .

items.title: A key report for where inflation stood in October comes out Tuesday. Here's what to expect
items.summary: The CPI headline reading is expected to show an increase of 0.3% while the core is forecast to increase 0.2%.
items.body: Falling gasoline prices provided some relief to consumers in October, but Federal Reserve officials are increasingly concerned that inflation pressures elsewhere in the economy are proving harder to contain. Prices at the pump declined by more than 4%, according to the Energy Information Administration, providing a respite from a surge that had added more than a dollar a gallon over the past year. However, the consumer price index for the month, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release Tuesday at 8:30 a.m., is expected to show only a slight let-up. Meanwhile, Fed officials say they are worried that inflation initially driven higher by President Donald Trump 's tariffs and the Iran war is proving more persistent than expected, with price pressures emerging in sectors beyond those directly affected by the shocks.

items.title: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
items.summary: Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.
items.body: US inflation rose at a faster-than-expected pace in October, according to official figures. Prices rose by 0.4% in the month, which was lower than the 0.6% increase in September. However, analysts had expected prices to rise by 0.3%, and the higher-than-expected pace could add to arguments for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next meeting in December. The new figures come a week after the midterm elections which were fought over cost-of-living pressures across the US. Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increases over time. For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%. Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI).

items.title: ‘Flying cars’ could launch in China next summer, maker of two-seat model says
items.summary: XPeng says its $300k low-altitude device will soon be ready for emergency services and recreational use in rural areas People could start taking trips in so-called flying cars in China as soon as next summer, the manufacturer of a two-seater vehicle with autopilot model has…
items.body: People could start taking trips in so-called flying cars in China as soon as next summer, the manufacturer of a two-seater vehicle with autopilot model has said. Deli Zhao, the chief executive of the Chinese flying car company XPeng, said the $300,000 (£225,000) low-altitude device would be ready for use by recreational users in rural locations and by emergency services in the second half of 2027. After 10 years of development including trials of flying motorbikes at the company’s Guangzhou base, it has been approved by China’s civil aviation authorities for limited use. The small cockpit is about the size of a Fiat 500 car and the vehicle is lifted into the air by six drone-like battery-powered propellers and steered by a simple joystick. It can also fly autonomously to a programmed destination, but Xhao, a trained pilot, claimed he could teach anyone to fly it in five minutes.

items.title: CoreWeave beats on revenue and lifts guidance, easing AI slowdown concerns
items.summary: CoreWeave's stock has been hammered heading into the neocloud's Q3 earnings report.
items.body: CoreWeave reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and lifted its 2026 guidance on Tuesday, showing that demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remains strong despite concerns of a market slowdown. The stock advanced in extended trading. The earnings announcement lands at a particularly volatile moment for CoreWeave and its neocloud peers, as the market sours on the AI trade and as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , the central figure in the global buildout, faces a scandal tied to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. CoreWeave's revenue soared 168% from about $1.36 billion a year earlier, according to a statement. The company recorded a net loss of $709 million, or $1.27 per share, compared to a net loss of $110 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings exclude stock-based compensation. Executives pushed up their forecast for 2026.

items.title: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash
items.summary: The contents of the calendar, including hair clips and keychains, have been widely criticised on social media.
items.body: Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering customers refunds for its $148 (£110) advent calendar which has been widely criticised on social media. The accessories advent calendar promised "twelve days of fun surprises" but has been mocked online for the quality of its contents, such as hair clips and keychains, with some comparing them to something you would find down the back of a sofa. A spokesperson for Skims has told a number of media outlets "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations" and the company has "personally contacted every customer" to offer a full refund or credit to put towards other products". The shapewear and clothing business was co-founded by Kardashian in 2019 and has made the reality TV star a billionaire, according to Forbes magazine. Skims was valued at $5bn in 2025 when it raised millions of dollars in new funding.

items.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in stock market flotation
items.summary: Claude chatbot developer had been reported to be aiming for $2tn IPO on Wall Street before investors cooled on AI Anthropic is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4tn (£1.1tn) in its imminent stock market flotation , short of the $2tn that had been expected before investors started…
items.body: Anthropic is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4tn (£1.1tn) in its imminent stock market flotation , short of the $2tn that had been expected before investors started to question the durability of the AI boom. The developer of the Claude chatbot was widely reported to be targeting a $2tn initial public offering on Wall Street but its sights have been set lower, according to a US regulatory filing on Tuesday. Anthropic is aiming to raise up to $64.4bn by selling 825m shares in the IPO priced up to $78 a share. The California-based company will also raise a further $26bn via a separate private placement deal ⁠with cornerstone investors including the Google parent, Alphabet, and the chipmaker Nvidia.

items.title: As China extends pause on rare earth controls, pricing and financing hold back EU supply push
items.summary: As Beijing announced a two-month extension to its rare earth export control pause, European industry insiders welcomed a positive change of mindset in the bloc’s efforts to reduce its dependency on imports of rare earths and other raw materials but cautioned that problems…
items.body: As Beijing announced a two-month extension to its rare earth export control pause, European industry insiders welcomed a positive change of mindset in the bloc’s efforts to reduce its dependency on imports of rare earths and other raw materials but cautioned that problems remained, especially in financing and regulations, while analysts warned the EU was running out of time. On Monday, the Ministry of Commerce in Beijing extended a pause on export controls covering several rare earths and related technologies, as well as lithium batteries and synthetic graphite anode material, until January.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield races back to 5% as inflation data, Waller comments drive rate hike expectations
items.summary: Treasury yields moved higher after a hotter-than-expected CPI report.
items.body: Treasury yields jumped on Tuesday after the U.S. consumer price index data for October came in hotter than expected . A mediocre auction of $42 billion in Treasury notes compounded the decline in bonds. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, car loans and credit card rates — traded above 5% before paring gains. It was last up 13 basis points at 4.992%. The 30-year Treasury bond yield, more sensitive to geopolitical developments, rose more than 9 basis points to 5.352%. The 2-year Treasury note yield, which closely tracks short-term Fed rate expectations, surged more than 18 basis points to 4.736%. The 10-year yield last traded above the 5% level earlier this month. In October, 10-year and 30-year yields hit 24-year highs . One basis point equals 0.01% or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.

items.title: I took Vinted to court to get my money back
items.summary: The BBC hears from Vinted sellers who describe difficulties accessing money held in their online wallets.
items.body: Mali Osmelak never imagined that selling clothes on Vinted would end with a court claim to recover almost £6,000. She started trading on the platform to earn an income while managing Crohn's disease and caring for her four-year-old daughter. But when she became a professional seller in March, she was unable to complete Vinted's verification process, leaving thousands of pounds inaccessible in her Vinted wallet. After several weeks of trying to resolve the issue, Mali took legal action. Vinted says sellers may be asked to complete verification checks to comply with legal and regulatory requirements and 98% of transactions are completed smoothly without needing help from its support team. Vinted is hugely popular in the UK with 17 million users. The online marketplace does not charge a fee to sellers for listing on there.

items.title: Falkland Islanders face ‘devastating consequences’ if Argentina blocks oil project, says UK
items.summary: Countries clash over Sea Lion project as Hamburg tribunal risks deepening sovereignty dispute The people of the Falkland Islands face “devastating consequences” if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and…
items.body: The people of the Falkland Islands face “devastating consequences” if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and Wales has told an international tribunal. Ellie Reeves, representing the British government at a hearing of the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos), said billions of pounds vital to the future of the British overseas territory would be lost. Reeves accused Argentina of surreptitiously seeking to pursue its longstanding sovereignty claims over the south Atlantic islands through an application to the tribunal, which is sitting over two days in Hamburg. Argentina is seeking a provisional ruling suspending the drilling for oil before further arbitration over the future of the project, which it claims poses an environmental risk.

items.title: Chinese investment in African manufacturing could change the world
items.summary: Africa is seeing a potentially historic transformation in its economic relationship with China. After two decades in which Chinese engagement was primarily associated with infrastructure construction, resource extraction and commodity trade, a new phase is emerging. Chinese…
items.body: Africa is seeing a potentially historic transformation in its economic relationship with China. After two decades in which Chinese engagement was primarily associated with infrastructure construction, resource extraction and commodity trade, a new phase is emerging. Chinese companies are increasingly establishing manufacturing operations on the continent, bringing capital, technology, production expertise and employment. East Africa, particularly Kenya and Tanzania, is becoming a principal destination for this industrial expansion. The significance of this development goes well beyond the growing volume of Chinese investment. It denotes a shift in the economic geography of China-Africa relations: from extracting resources and building infrastructure to producing goods, developing supply chains and accessing expanding consumer markets. The figures illustrate the scale of the transition.

items.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78, looks to start trading Nov. 19, sources say
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO is expected to come roughly five months after Elon Musk took SpaceX public in a record offering.
items.body: Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 and $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the 5-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut. The company is planning to price on Nov. 18 and trade on Nov. 19, according to people familiar with the details who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is targeting retail allocation of about 20%, the people said, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors. At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO.

items.title: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security
items.summary: Huang, who is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, is far more important to the future of the world order than other tech bosses.
items.body: Jensen Huang has the air of the late Steve Jobs about him. I have interviewed both, and the up-close charisma - and occasionally scratchy genius - is shared. Both sported a signature item of black clothing, although Huang opts for a leather jacket rather than the Apple founder's turtle neck. Both are innovators revered in the tech world. However, Huang is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy . Everything you have heard about Artificial Intelligence (AI) over the past few months - good, bad, revolutionary and catastrophic - is dependent on having the most powerful frontier AI models. In turn they depend on the most powerful microchips, and for years that has been this very company, Nvidia, led by Huang, and his technology rooted in repurposed games graphics and the manufacturing prowess of Taiwan.

items.title: Britain willing to discuss paying into EU to join electricity market, says minister
items.summary: Hamish Falconer says UK has ‘not accepted principle’ of linking electricity trade to ‘cohesion fund’ but two sides will discuss issue Britain is willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity…
items.body: Britain is willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market, according to the minister in charge of renegotiating the bilateral relationship. Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, told the Guardian he was sure the two sides would discuss the issue after this month’s summit, as ministers look to deepen ties with the union over the next few years. Andy Burnham, the prime minister, has said he wants a much closer relationship with the EU in the future, even raising the possibility of rejoining as a full member. But while senior figures in Brussels have said they are keen to discuss such an idea, they also want to see the UK begin to start paying for access to the European schemes it says it wants.

items.title: China’s imports outpace exports in October amid efforts to address record imbalance
items.summary: China’s trade momentum remained strong in October despite a strengthening of the yuan, sending its year-to-date trade surplus above US$1 trillion amid rising scrutiny from Western countries over the size of the gap. Supported by the continuing technology cycle and a rebound in…
items.body: China’s trade momentum remained strong in October despite a strengthening of the yuan, sending its year-to-date trade surplus above US$1 trillion amid rising scrutiny from Western countries over the size of the gap. Supported by the continuing technology cycle and a rebound in demand as US-China relations improved, the country’s exports rose by 35.2 per cent year on year to US$412.33 billion last month, according to Chinese customs data released on Tuesday, compared with the 36.3 per cent growth recorded in September. The reading beat the 33.25 per cent growth forecast by economists in a poll by financial data provider Wind. Imports rose 41.6 per cent to US$307.05 billion, the fastest growth recorded since May 2021 and well above Wind’s forecast of 30.36 per cent. The faster growth in imports narrowed the monthly trade surplus to US$105.28 billion, from US$133.53 billion in September.

items.title: U.S. gas prices fall below $4 for the first time since July
items.summary: Americans may finally find some relief at the pump.
items.body: The national average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, reaching $3.9788 on Tuesday, according to AAA . Prices are down about 17 cents from a week ago and nearly 39 cents from a month ago. The decline comes after energy inflation slowed significantly in October. Energy prices increased 0.7% during the month, a far cry from the 5.2% surge seen in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics . The BLS' gasoline index increased 1% over the month, after advancing 9.1% in September. Bespoke Investment Group pointed out that gasoline prices also tend to decline at this time of the year, making part of the recent relief seasonal.

items.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
items.body: US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy. Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign. "I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Speaking later at a White House press briefing, Trump told reporters, "I know the FBI is looking into" the affair but did not give further details on the investigation, or confirm when it was launched.

items.title: Pharma firms’ focus on weight-loss drugs could put insulin supply at risk, experts warn
items.summary: GLP-1 products such as Ozempic and Mounjaro spread but many in poorer countries struggle to get basic diabetes treatment The gold rush into GLP-1 weight-loss drugs risks diverting pharmaceutical firms’ attention away from diabetes treatments such as insulin, the head of the…
items.body: The gold rush into GLP-1 weight-loss drugs risks diverting pharmaceutical firms’ attention away from diabetes treatments such as insulin, the head of the Access to Medicine Foundation has warned. GLP-1 blockbuster medications such as Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro have revolutionised obesity and diabetes treatment but there has been a greater focus by companies on weight loss, according to a report from the Netherlands-based non-profit group. The group warned that many people cannot even get hold of basic insulin, critical for people with type 1 diabetes, and many countries were struggling to access GLP-1 medications at all – as the explosion in their popularity continues since the weight-loss jab Wegovy launched in 2021.

items.title: The superpower battle over energy – and what it means for your bills
items.summary: A tug-of-war between China and the US could have a big impact on energy costs, but who will win?
items.body: A gas rig in the North Sea. An oil field in Texas. A solar panel factory in China. They can feel a world away, but your energy bill says otherwise. In January, it could jump by more than a quarter – around £460 extra a year for the typical UK household – according to the latest forecasts from the big suppliers British Gas, EDF and E.ON. For the second time in four years, a war thousands of miles away is landing in British inboxes. Since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, oil and gas prices have soared. Winter is expected to push them higher still: demand for gas is rising just as Europe's winter gas stores are at their lowest since records began in 2011. And there's a bigger threat looming over all of this: the warming climate.

items.title: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’
items.summary: Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is…
items.body: Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over” . Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end. Europe’s benchmark Stoxx 600 index gained 0.9% to 662.54, hovering near a record high, which it had hit in early August on hopes for a peace deal in the Middle East. Airline stocks rose amid hopes that easing tensions could lead to lower fuel costs, with Lufthansa 1.8% ahead and Air France-KLM up 1.2%. In London, the FTSE 100 index climbed 45 points, or 0.4%, to 10,828.

items.title: House begins voting on Hegseth impeachment measure

items.body: The House of Representatives began voting Tuesday afternoon on a key procedural measure that could lead to the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The vote comes a week after Democrats trounced Republicans in the first congressional election since the war with Iran started in late February. Hegseth faces eight articles of impeachment filed by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., on Monday. Massie accuses Hegseth of waging war in contravention of Congress, carrying out extrajudicial killings tied to boat strikes in the Caribbean against purported drug smugglers and suppressing free speech by targeting Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., a military veteran. Massie is a libertarian who lost his Republican primary in May after clashing with President Donald Trump .

items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
items.body: He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work. At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was. But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked. She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead. "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial. She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick. Something he denied in court. That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia?
items.summary: Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young…
items.body: For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large. He’s also made it a family business. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm. While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares. But Huang’s image as a family man has been shattered as of Sunday. After the New York Times revealed at the end of October that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence asset who he had developed a close relationship with, he admitted in a letter to employees on Sunday that he had been having an affair.

items.title: FDA warns of vision loss risk linked to popular GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy, Zepbound
items.summary: The agency has found evidence of a potential increased risk of a rare eye condition linked to the use of GLP-1 drugs used for weight management and diabetes.
items.body: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is requiring new safety warnings on all GLP-1 drugs after finding evidence of a potential increased risk of a rare eye condition, the agency said on Monday. The condition, which can cause sudden vision loss, known as nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), is rare, and a causal relationship has not been established. The FDA is requiring the makers of all GLP-1 medications to add a warning about the potential increased risk of NAION associated with use of these medications, it said. NAION is a condition that can result in sudden decreased vision, including permanent vision loss. It is caused by decreased blood flow to the front part of the ​optic nerve — the underlying cause is not completely understood, however. NAION cases have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 products, the FDA said.

items.body: C all it tough love. Only without any of the love bit. Let’s face it. There comes a time in every Conservative politician’s life when you have to say enough is enough. That it’s just not fair on the rest of us. Now, MPs might just have enjoyed a five-day mini-recess, but they deserve every minute’s free time they get. Because they clearly work far harder than everyone else. But on a Tuesday morning it sticks in the throat to think of people lying around at home, being paid to have disabilities that exist mainly in their imaginations, while you have to give a speech in central London. items.body: Ten days after Alphabet shares experienced their worst one-day drubbing in its history, the search, media and AI giant has barely retraced a faction of its nearly $500 billion in lost market capitalization, having rallied just a paltry 1.5%. The muted recovery stands out for a company that posted its 13th straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth in the same report, with Google Cloud revenue more than doubling. Alphabet's earnings were the first major crack to appear in the AI trade and foreshadowed a series of volatile events for the complex, including the election and the growing scandal enveloping Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Still, a bullish case for Alphabet rests not in its post-earnings concerns being unfounded, but rather on its growth being strong enough to withstand them.

items.summary: California saw the most expensive opposition campaign in its history as funding of political campaigns broke records in the US midterms In the hours after polls closed on election day, tech industry players began praising Sergey Brin, the co-founder of Google, on social media.…
items.body: In the hours after polls closed on election day, tech industry players began praising Sergey Brin , the co-founder of Google, on social media. “Huge thanks to Sergey Brin here,” wrote Garry Tan, the CEO of Y Combinator. Venture capitalist Ilya Sukhar posted : “God bless Sergey Brin.” And David Marcus, a crypto entrepreneur, simply wrote : “Hero.” They were all referring to Brin’s instrumental role in the defeat of California’s wealth tax ballot measure, known as Proposition 40. The proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires in the state was defeated by just over five points . Simultaneously, an opposition initiative that would ban any taxation on billionaire wealth, Proposition 42, put on the ballot by Brin and a cohort of the state’s ultra-rich, is poised to pass. Brin, whose net worth is about $230bn, contributed at least $132m to the fight – more than any other donor.

items.title: Californians reject wealth tax for billionaires
items.summary: Proposition 40 targeted Californian billionaires with a 5% tax on their total wealth, including assets such as shares as well as income.
items.body: The ballot proposal would have levied a one-time tax on the state's mega wealthy to help fund healthcare. It took nearly a week of counting votes after the midterm election to determine a projection on the measure. There are about 200 billionaires in the state, including Meta's Mark Zuckerberg , reality television star Kim Kardashian and media mogul Oprah Winfrey. Proposition 40 targeted Californians with a wealth of more than $1.1bn (£800m) with a 5% tax on their total wealth, including assets such as shares as well as income. It failed amid divisions among Democrats and labour unions. Had it passed, experts believe it would have been the world's first wealth tax targeting billionaires. The tax would have raised about $100bn to make up for federal funding cuts to healthcare in California as a result of President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.

The embattled chip giant briefly dipped below $4 trillion in market cap during afternoon trading, but bounced back to close above that level. Nvidia last cleared the $4 trillion benchmark on July 9, 2025. Shares closed more than 4% lower on Monday, the day after Huang told staff in an email that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and had "fallen short" of his responsibilities as CEO. He reportedly had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed , an Nvidia customer. items.title: Australia considers criminal penalties for rogue AI in wake of OpenAI hack
items.summary: AI safety regulator will also be created after a rogue OpenAI agent hacked government websites.
items.body: Australia plans to create a new AI safety regulator and has flagged criminal penalties for tech companies who do not comply, months after an OpenAI hack. In September, Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that a rogue OpenAI agent had "infiltrated" a government health website and other systems, and criticised the company for taking months to tell them about the hack. On Tuesday, he released the 18 recommendations made after a "rapid review" into the breaches including new safety and security standards for AI companies such as mandatory reporting of hacks. AI brings opportunities, he said, but Australia must prepare for the "new risks" from this "rapidly advancing technology". "The law needs to get ahead of and, in some cases, make sure that it catches up with, what is a very fast changing world," Albanese said.

items.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.body: A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing.

items.title: The French fridge hacks were relatively unsophisticated. An AI-enabled attack would raise the stakes
items.summary: ‘Not particularly complex’ defrosting hack has been attributed to Iran, with presumption it is linked to others across Europe Iranian hackers like to send a message. In 2023 a state-backed group interrupted TV streaming services in the United Arab Emirates to broadcast a…
items.body: In 2023 a state-backed group interrupted TV streaming services in the United Arab Emirates to broadcast a deepfake report on the war in Gaza. Some refrigerators had their temperature turned up so high they caught fire. ‌In the hours after the hack, supermarket employees dumped piles of perished meat and melted ice-cream into rubbish containers.

items.title: How to get the buzz back on Britain’s high streets | Letters
items.summary: Readers respond to an article about the decline of town centres Sammy Gecsoyler’s report from Rotherham ( ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?, 4 November ) tells the story in its dates. One out-of-town retail park in…
items.body: Sammy Gecsoyler’s report from Rotherham ( ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?, 4 November ) tells the story in its dates. One out-of-town retail park in Britain in 1981; 385 by 1996. Parkgate opened in 1987 and MPs warned that it would disembowel towns and villages. It did. Rotherham town centre is now 24% vacant, while retail park vacancy nationally sits at 4.8%. That is not a mystery. It is 40 years of planning policy. We have since gone one step further by making home delivery cheaper than retail parks. Up to 3bn parcels a year now land on British doorsteps and not one of them passes through a town centre. Andy Burnham’s £210m for high streets is welcome, but is a one-off against a structural problem. What a town centre needs is a reason for people to walk into it again, every week, without being told to.

items.body: Qantas will outsource 850 local corporate jobs to consulting giant Accenture with most roles moving to India as the airline fast-tracks AI investment. In an internal email to staff on Tuesday, the Australian company's CEO Vanessa Hudson said "this is hard news for some and I'm sorry for the uncertainty it brings". The job cuts will begin mid-2027, she said, and start with finance, procurement, people and marketing roles shifting "mostly" to teams in India and "some in Australia" as the firm seeks to modernise its IT systems. Hudson said the "scale and speed of change in technology and AI is something none of us has seen in our lifetime", and it was in talks with unions and staff on the plans. The move comes days after the airline provided a market update, flagging fare increases and flight cuts amid higher fuel costs.

items.title: UK social media ban expansion for under-16s could cover YouTube Kids

items.body: A substantial expansion of the social media ban for under-16s could inadvertently lead to a ban on YouTube Kids and other sites that had been thought exempt, sources briefed on the government’s proposals have said. One source close to the talks said the regulations now under consideration meant up to 150 platforms, including games platforms such as Lego Play, could be covered by the ban, which is set to come into force in March. The regulations will be sent for cabinet signoff this week, and the culture secretary, Lisa Nandy , is expected to lay them in parliament in December. Ministers are understood to be keen for a catch-all approach that limits ban workarounds. Critics of Australia’s social media prohibition say teenagers have switched to new platforms or found innovative ways of messaging using other seemingly innocuous sites.

items.title: Trump sees opening for Ukraine peace deal, but key questions remain ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
items.summary: President Trump signaled optimism for the end of Russia's war in Ukraine ahead of trilateral negotiation talks on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi.
items.body: President Donald Trump said there was increasing willingness from both Russia and Ukraine to end the war, as representatives from Kyiv and Moscow headed to Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for the first peace talks since February. Speaking to reporters at the White House on Monday, Trump said both sides were battle-weary, more than four and a half years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. "We're also seeing a very strong inclination to end Russia and Ukraine [ war]," Trump said ahead of the U.S.-brokered negotiations, adding that, "We're involved in that because I want to see people stop getting killed again." His comments followed a U.S. official’s assessment that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing some flexibility over a possible exchange of territory, according to Reuters.

items.title: SoftBank swings to first-half loss as AI hopes face new setbacks
items.body: TOKYO -- SoftBank Group on Tuesday swung to a first-half net loss, as it faces growing uncertainty over its ambitious artificial intelligence strategy following political setbacks in the U.S. and regulatory hurdles in China.

items.title: Britons stockpiling water and food tins but not panic buying, figures show
items.summary: Shoppers appear to have taken government’s Be Ready campaign seriously, retail analysts say British shoppers have been stocking up on essentials such as bottled water, tinned goods and hand sanitiser, but did not panic buy after the government advised people to prepare for…
items.body: British shoppers have been stocking up on essentials such as bottled water, tinned goods and hand sanitiser, but did not panic buy after the government advised people to prepare for emergencies, shopping data has shown. Sales of essentials jumped in the 10 days after the government launched its Be Ready campaign , which encourages households to prepare for up to three days in the event of disruption to essential services from incidents such as cyber-attacks or extreme weather. In the 10 days after the campaign launch, sales of hand sanitiser surged by 83% compared with the same period last year, while sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods went up 37%, according to Worldpanel by Numerator’s monthly grocery report for Great Britain.

items.title: Anthropic's trillion-dollar IPO is coming, but retail investors could have owned AI stock much earlier
items.summary: Anthropic is on target for an IPO that could value the AI company at over $1.4 trillion. Investors had multiple ways to buy the stock much earlier.
items.body: Anthropic is set to go public next week, with a potential date of Nov. 19 for an initial public offering that could value the AI giant on a fully diluted basis at over $1.4 trillion. For many retail investors, the IPO may be the first chance they have to own Anthropic and even that ownership event will be out of reach with limited shares allocated to retail brokerage firms. But there were ways for retail investors to own Anthropic shares at a much earlier date. Investors may also be able to get in on the next hot IPO well before listing day. There are several ways to do this, though it can depend on whether you're an accredited investor under SEC guidelines when investing directly in a private company versus accessing a privately held stock through a diversified fund.

items.title: Honda bets on hybrids as mainstay of US electrification into early 2030s
items.body: TOKYO -- Honda Motor expects that hybrid vehicles will continue to be the main driver of electrification in the U.S. into the early years of the next decade as the Japanese automaker is betting on the technology while making a hasty retreat from the costly electric vehicle push.

items.title: Law on 'holiday hunger' passed by Stormont assembly
items.summary: A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities.
items.body: A law aimed at helping lower income families with food costs during school holidays has been passed by the Northern Ireland Assembly. The Holiday Meal Payments Bill seeks to create a new payment for families whose children receive free school meals to help with food costs outside of term time. A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities. Education Minister Paul Givan described the bill as "fiscally reckless", warning it would cost £20m to £30m a year and lead to cuts elsewhere within his Stormont department. Baker said that "poverty isn't green and orange" and the passage of the bill would support thousands of children "across all of our communities".

items.title: Young people in UK hit by ‘low-gear economy’, warns Bank of England deputy
items.summary: Exclusive: Iran war has fuelled energy price rise and clouded outlook, driving up unemployment, says Clare Lombardelli Young people in Britain are bearing the brunt of a “low-gear economy” as employers hold back from hiring amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East, a…
items.body: Young people in Britain are bearing the brunt of a “low-gear economy” as employers hold back from hiring amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East, a deputy governor of the Bank of England has warned. Clare Lombardelli, the Bank’s deputy governor for monetary policy, said the unfolding conflict, which has triggered a surge in energy prices and clouded the outlook for the economy, was contributing to an increase in youth unemployment. “What you see is the cost falling on young people, so you can see this rapid rise in the number of young people who are struggling to find jobs,” she said. Against a highly volatile backdrop, she also warned Threadneedle Street was preparing for a “live” decision on interest rates next month after it increased the cost of borrowing last week for the first time in three years .

items.title: Brent crude briefly dips below $90 for first time since August on Iran hopes
items.summary: President Trump said Monday he thought the conflict was "going to be ending fairly soon," but some analysts still see little chance of a lasting peace deal.
items.body: International oil benchmark Brent crude briefly fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August on Tuesday as comments from U.S. President Donald Trump fueled hopes for an end to Washington's nearly nine-month conflict with Iran. Brent, the price gauge for around 80% of global crude, settled down 1.17% at $91.49 a barrel. At its session low, the international benchmark slid to $89.16. U.S. WTI crude fell 0.93% to settle at $86.04 a barrel. Trump said on Monday that the war with Iran could end "fairly soon" and that Tehran was "talking very politely" with Washington. "We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said at the White House following a meeting with Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani. "Iran militarily is effectively over," Trump told reporters.
